title: What Each File Wants
dek: There is no best compressor, only a best match between what a file is and how it will be read. A measured field guide, October 2026: JSON at rest and on the wire, small messages and dictionaries, binary encodings, config files, logs, tables, images, audio and video — which codec, which level or quality, when a format beats a compressor, and when to leave a file alone.
byline: 9 October 2026 · Every recommendation backed by a measurement on this machine with recorded tool versions, or by a cited source; the XO examples are read from its tree
description: A measured field guide to compressing JSON, config files, logs, tabular data, images, audio and video in 2026: codecs, levels, dictionaries, columnar encodings and media codecs, and when not to compress.
og_description: zstd vs brotli vs gzip on JSON, dictionaries for small messages, CBOR and MessagePack vs compressed JSON, config files that grow, logs by block size, Parquet vs gzip'd CSV, AVIF and JPEG XL, Opus and FLAC, x264 vs x265 vs SVT-AV1 by VMAF — all measured, October 2026.
twitter_description: No best compressor, only the right match. JSON, config, logs, tables, images, audio and video — measured, with the codec and level each one wants.
